summary.name: Yaak
summary.one_liner: Yaak is a local-first desktop API client for HTTP, GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket, and SSE that stores requests as Git-versioned files on your machine.
use_cases: testing REST and GraphQL APIs during development
sharing API requests with a team through Git
keeping API requests offline and private
letting AI agents work with existing API requests
migrating collections from Postman or Insomnia
summary.what_it_does:
Yaak is a desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux that sends API requests over HTTP, GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket, and Server-Sent Events. Each request, folder, and environment is saved as one YAML file, and the built-in Git UI handles branching, committing, and diffing. Requests can be chained and values reused without scripts, and every redirect, header, and detail can be inspected. Plugins can extend auth, importers, and template functions. A CLI and MCP server plugin let AI agents work on the same workspace files shown in the app.</what_it_does>
<parameter name="pricing">freemium
notable: Requests stored as one YAML file each, versioned with Git, with a built-in Git UI
Desktop app built with Rust and Tauri; no account and no automatic cloud sync
Secrets encrypted with keys from the OS keychain; zero telemetry from the desktop app
CLI and MCP server plugin so agents like Claude Code and Cursor can use the same workspace
caveats: Commercial use requires a paid license after a 30-day trial (Individual $79/user/year, Business $149/user/year, Individual Lifetime $399/user one-time)
Free for personal use only, per the page
Team features such as SSO, SCIM, and seat licensing are paid
